answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake in a vault before it can submit work; the protocol randomly selects a few submissions for costly verification, and a proven duplicate identity forfeits the stake. Splitting one operator across many identities therefore multiplies the capital tied up and the chance of losing it, while gaining no extra influence unless each identity also earns a history of verified contributions. A relic from an older account or a willow-named profile gives no exemption: the cost follows the stake and the evidence, not the name.
